rhel.name: RHEL family (Anaconda installer)
rhel.nvidia: Use the vendor repositories (RPM Fusion on Fedora, ELRepo or NVIDIA's CUDA repo on RHEL clones). With Secure Boot on, drivers must be signed and the key enrolled (MOK).
install_steps: Boot the USB stick and choose the Install entry.
Pick language and keyboard, then open 'Installation Destination'.
Select the target disk and choose 'Custom' (or 'Advanced Custom') to apply the layout shown above. Keep the LVM scheme.
Open 'Software Selection' and pick Server, Server with GUI, Workstation or Minimal Install.
Set network/hostname, time zone, root password and a user account.
Click 'Begin Installation', wait, then reboot and remove the USB stick.
post_steps: Update the system: sudo dnf update
Enable extra repositories if needed (EPEL on Alma/Rocky/CentOS Stream/Oracle, subscription-manager on RHEL).
Check the boot loader is the default entry: efibootmgr -v

debian.name: Debian/Ubuntu family
debian.nvidia: Tick 'Install third-party software' in the installer, or use the Additional/Proprietary Drivers tool after install. With Secure Boot on, accept the MOK enrollment prompt on first reboot.
install_steps: Boot the USB stick and choose 'Install' (or 'Try', then launch the installer from the desktop).
Pick language, keyboard and network. Tick the option for third-party drivers/codecs if offered.

At the installation type step choose 'Something else' / 'Manual partitioning' / 'Custom' and create the layout shown above. Choose 'Erase disk' only if you do not need a custom layout. For dual boot choose 'Install alongside' or use the free space.
Set the boot loader target to the whole disk (BIOS) or leave it on the EFI partition (UEFI).
Choose time zone and create your user account.
Install, then reboot and remove the USB stick when asked.
post_steps: Update: sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade
Install proprietary drivers if you use NVIDIA or Broadcom Wi-Fi.
Check the boot menu shows all installed systems: sudo update-grub

arch.name: Arch family
arch.nvidia: Install nvidia / nvidia-open (or nvidia-dkms for custom kernels) and nvidia-utils. Manjaro and Garuda detect hardware drivers during or after install.
install_steps: Boot the live USB and wait for the desktop (or the installer menu).
Launch the installer, pick language, region and keyboard.
At 'Partitions' choose 'Manual partitioning' and create the layout shown above (or 'Erase disk' for the default layout).
Create your user account and choose the desktop/package set if asked.
Review the summary, install, then reboot and remove the USB stick.
post_steps: Install microcode for your CPU (intel-ucode or amd-ucode) if the installer did not.
Set up regular SSD trim: sudo systemctl enable --now fstrim.timer

suse.name: SUSE family
suse.nvidia: Add the NVIDIA repository (YaST Software Repositories or 'zypper addrepo') and install the matching driver. With Secure Boot on, enroll the MOK key when prompted.
install_steps: Boot the USB stick and choose 'Installation'.
Pick language, keyboard and product/edition.
At storage setup choose 'Expert Partitioner' / 'Custom' and apply the layout shown above, or accept the guided proposal (Btrfs root with snapshots, separate /home on larger disks).
Select the desktop/software pattern, then set time zone and create your user.
Review the summary, install, then reboot and remove the USB stick.
post_steps: Refresh and update: sudo zypper refresh && sudo zypper update (use 'zypper dup' on Tumbleweed).
Install multimedia codecs from the Packman repository if you need them.
Learn snapshots: sudo snapper list (you can roll back from the boot menu).

independent.name: Independent / manual install
independent.nvidia: Follow the distribution's wiki page for NVIDIA drivers. Driver packaging differs a lot between these distributions.
post_steps: Update the system with the distribution's package manager.
Check the boot loader entry and test a reboot before removing the install medium.

generic.name: Unknown / generic
generic.nvidia: Check the distribution's documentation for driver installation.
install_steps: Boot the USB stick and start the installer.
At partitioning choose manual/custom and create the layout shown above.
Create a user, install, reboot and remove the USB stick.
post_steps: Update the system and verify the boot loader.
